Report a saved investigation

Source: R/investigation-report.R
investigation_report.Rd

investigation_report() computes a shareable report from a saved investigation without starting the app. It applies the saved view's filters to the saved evidence and analysis, exactly as scans_app() does when it opens the same investigation, and returns the resulting tables. write_investigation_report() renders them as one standalone HTML file or as Markdown; format() returns the same text.

Usage

investigation_report(
  x,
  reviews = NULL,
  app_url = NULL,
  include_users = FALSE,
  include_errors = FALSE,
  verify = TRUE
)

write_investigation_report(
  x,
  path,
  format = NULL,
  max_evidence = 100L,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'scans_investigation_report'
format(x, format = c("markdown", "html"), max_evidence = 100L, ...)

Arguments

x

A saved investigation from investigation_snapshot() or read_investigation(). A TrajectoryBundle is captured first with investigation_snapshot() and its defaults. For write_investigation_report() and format(), a report.

reviews

Optional list of review_case() values made from this investigation's snapshot. Their adjudicated status is reported beside the evidence they refer to.

app_url

Optional address of a scans_app() deployment: an http:// or https:// host and path, with no credentials, query, or fragment. Without it the report has anchors only.

include_users

Whether to print user identifiers and the values of free-form source details. Defaults to FALSE.

include_errors

Whether to print the most frequent recorded error text per tool. Defaults to FALSE, which prints the count only.

verify

Whether to recompute the snapshot and revision identifiers and refuse an investigation they no longer describe. Defaults to TRUE. Use FALSE only for a value just returned by read_investigation() or investigation_snapshot().

path

File to write. The extension chooses the format unless format is given: .html or .htm for HTML, .md for Markdown.

format

"html" or "markdown".

max_evidence

Largest number of trajectories listed per pattern. The rendered report says when it lists fewer than it counted; the evidence table always holds them all.

overwrite

Whether to replace an existing file. Defaults to FALSE.

...

Unused.

Value

investigation_report() returns a scans_investigation_report: a list of ordinary tibbles and scope details.

  • scope: counts in scope, filters in words, the time window, the source read, snapshot identifiers, scanner settings, and what links cannot restore.

  • headline: one row of counts with their denominators, including n_assessed and n_not_assessed.

  • patterns: one row per finding type with affected trajectories, the number the scan assessed, the share of those affected (NA when it assessed none), and first and last occurrence.

  • tools, models, and, when requested, users: breakdowns. Findings in a model or user are counted over its n_assessed trajectories.

  • measures: each resource measure by recording coverage.

  • coverage: trajectories per scanner and assessment status.

  • losses: capture losses by field and reason.

  • trajectories: the cohort, one row per trajectory, with its class.

  • evidence: one row per finding with trajectory, turn, and event identities, its anchor in the rendered report, and links.

  • reviews: one row per supplied review case.

    write_investigation_report() returns the report invisibly. format() returns Markdown lines or one HTML string.

Details

The report states its scope (application, time window, every active filter, and what the source read covered), headline counts with their denominators, patterns with reach, tool failures, resource measurements with recording coverage, capture limits and losses, and the evidence behind each pattern. It never runs a scanner, calls a model, or contacts the source.

What the report can and cannot establish

Findings describe recorded behavior. A trajectory with no findings is reported as clean only when a selected scan could assess it; one that no scan could assess is counted as not assessed. A measurement that was not recorded is printed as unknown, never as zero. No findings does not establish success, and complete recording of the loaded records does not establish that the source captured everything.

Content

The report contains identities and scanner explanations, not transcript text: no message text, tool arguments, or tool results. A scanner() writes its own explanations, which the report prints as written, so a custom scanner that quotes the transcript puts that text in the report; the report then says which scans' explanations it prints. Tool names, model names, and trajectory, turn, and event identifiers do appear. Recorded error strings are often tool-result text, so the tool table counts errors without their text unless include_errors = TRUE. User identifiers are omitted unless include_users = TRUE; a text filter that matches a user identifier is then described without its term. Review rationales and expected behavior are free text and are never printed.

Source details a caller recorded with the investigation print their values only for the fields a source reader records about its read (read_at, from, to, n, spans, spans_total, max_spans, truncated, incomplete, conversations_found, conversations, files, and lines_dropped). Any other field is free-form and may name a person, so it is listed by name with its value withheld unless include_users = TRUE.

Integrity

The report checks the investigation's structure and evidence references, and recomputes the snapshot and revision identifiers to check that they still describe the content, so an investigation edited in R after it was read is refused rather than reported under its original identifiers. Recomputing them hashes the whole investigation, which on a large one takes longer than the report. A caller that has just read or built the value can pass verify = FALSE; the report then labels its identifiers as not re-verified, and says so beside any review cases matched by them. Build a changed revision with investigation_snapshot() rather than editing a saved value.

Links

With app_url, each trajectory and event links to that app. A link sets the filters the report names and clears every other filter in the app that opens it. It reopens exactly the reported cohort when that app serves this saved investigation; an app reading the live source applies the same filters to whatever it holds then. The report prints this, and names any filter a link cannot carry, under its scope.

Examples

bundle <- TrajectoryBundle(
  data.frame(trajectory_id = "run-1", source_type = "manual",
             status = "failed"),
  data.frame(), data.frame()
)
saved <- investigation_snapshot(bundle, application = "Support assistant")
report <- investigation_report(saved)
report$headline[c("n", "n_assessed", "n_findings")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>       n n_assessed n_findings
#>   <int>      <int>      <int>
#> 1     1          1          1
report$evidence[c("scan", "trajectory_id")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   scan             trajectory_id
#>   <chr>            <chr>        
#> 1 trajectory_error run-1        

if (requireNamespace("htmltools", quietly = TRUE)) {
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  write_investigation_report(report, path)
}
